title: MOCHA: Discovering Multi-Order Dynamic Causal Structure in Temporal Point Processes
claim: Real-world event sequences hide causal structure that changes over time and includes indirect multi-hop influences, which static first-order graphs miss.
layout: 2 stacked rows: timeline on top, four time-indexed graph panels below
description: The figure has two horizontal bands. The top band, labeled 'Event Sequence', is a timeline arrow running left to right. Four colored rounded boxes sit on it at times t1 to t4: Elevated Creatinine (orange), Hypertension (blue), Troponin Abnormal (green) and Elevated CRP (red). The bottom band, labeled 'Casual Graph', has four dashed rounded panels, one under each timestamp. Each panel contains the same four color-matched nodes. The node for the current event is bold. Arrows between nodes appear as time advances. At t2, creatinine points to hypertension. At t3, arrows run from creatinine and from hypertension to troponin. At t4, hypertension and troponin both point to CRP, so indirect multi-hop paths form. The eye goes first to the colorful timeline, then down to the growing graphs.
caption: Illustration of an event sequence and its time-varying causal graphs in clinical settings. Multi-order paths capture indirect influences over time.
abstract: Discovering complex causal dependencies in temporal point processes (TPPs) is critical for modeling real-world event sequences. Existing methods typically rely on static or first-order causal structures, overlooking the multi-order and time-varying nature of causal relationships. In this paper, we propose MOCHA, a novel framework for discovering multi-order dynamic causality in TPPs. MOCHA characterizes multi-order influences as multi-hop causal paths over a latent time-evolving graph. To model such dynamics, we introduce a time-varying directed acyclic graph (DAG) with learnable structural weights, where acyclicity and sparsity constraints are enforced to ensure structural validity. We design an end-to-end differentiable framework that jointly models causal discovery and TPP dynamics, enabling accurate event prediction and revealing interpretable structures. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that MOCHA not only achieves state-of-the-art performance in event prediction, but also reveals meaningful and interpretable causal structures.
